j6.1: The stream x for all words, [T, 4096]. Its size has grown through earlier blocks.
j6.2: A copy of each row is rescaled so that its size becomes 1. The direction is kept.
j6.3: h, the same shape as x. The stream x itself is untouched.
j6.4: Attention works best with inputs at an even scale. Normalizing only the copy keeps the straight path through the stream clean.
j6.5: h for this word and all the words before it.
j6.6: The query is compared with earlier keys, the scores become percentages, and the values are mixed by those percentages. Wo turns the mix into the stream’s format.
j6.7: One contribution per word, with information from other words.
j6.8: The only place where words can affect each other.
j6.9: x = x + contribution, number by number.
j6.10: x, which now carries context. Shape unchanged.
j6.11: Nothing is overwritten. What was in the stream before is still there.
j6.12: The MLP also wants an even scale.
j6.13: h for one word at a time. No other words are visible.
j6.14: Expand to 14,336 neurons, let through the ones whose pattern matches, compress back to 4096.
j6.15: One contribution per word: what the model knows about what was fetched.
j6.16: Here stored knowledge is used to draw conclusions.
j6.17: x, ready for the next block.
j6.18: The block is done. The next block repeats the same six stations with new weights.
j6.24: a noun that “den” can refer to
j6.27: Query = the search: {{q}}. Keys = the video titles. Values = the content. “den” does not get a single video, but {{p1}}% {{d1}}, {{p2}}% {{d2}} and a bit of the rest. In the model, query, key and value are vectors, and the “titles” are not words but numbers.
j6.28: Three versions of each word’s vector, computed with the learned matrices Wq, Wk and Wv. Q, K and V are therefore not weights; they are computed anew for every token.
j6.29: In the example: q for “den” = [1,5; 0,5]. Keys: Katten [2; 0], satt [0; 1], den [1; 1].
j6.31: Every query is multiplied with every key. If they point the same way, the number gets large. The result is a score table: how well each word matches every other one.
j6.32: 3.00 for Katten, 0.50 for satt, 2.00 for den.
j6.33: Dot products of long vectors get large. Without scaling, softmax would put almost all weight on a single word, and the model would learn poorly. d is 128 in Llama.
j6.35: Scores against words that come later are set to minus infinity. After softmax their weight becomes exactly zero. The formula is usually written without the mask, but decoder-only models always include it.
j6.36: In the example there are no later words, so nothing is masked.
j6.38: Each row is turned into positive numbers that sum to 1. Large differences in score become large differences in weight.
j6.40: Each word gets a mix of all the values, weighted by the percentages. Then Wo mixes the 32 heads together, and the result is added to the stream.
j6.46: Compared with 14,336 patterns (48 shown). Each bar is how well one pattern matches.
j6.47: SiLU dampens everything that does not match. Only some neurons stay clearly lit.
j6.48: The neurons that lit up are translated back into 4096 numbers: the MLP’s contribution.

j6.51: No key matches fully, so no value is written. The neurons need both properties at the same time, which only works thanks to the non-linear dimmer.
